notes: The RTL line 343 assigns smp.scl from smp.sda_sreg rather than smp.scl_sreg, despite the signal name and the surrounding sampling logic.
The conceptual list describes RX FIFO storage with no Held Lines; the storage is inside the black-box rx_fifo_inst and is observed through rx_fifo.rdata at lines 277 and 190.

points.reason: A bus write changes ctrl.enable, and its value can disable FIFO operation, sampling, engine progress, and the clock-enable output.
The enable-controlled clear can clear the receive FIFO and prevent received data from remaining available.
The enable-controlled clear can clear the transmit FIFO and prevent queued transfers.
When enable is low, sampling is stopped and the synchronizer stages are forced to inactive values.
The engine returns to or remains in idle when enable is cleared, preventing normal TWD transfers.
The enable gates irq_o, so clearing it can suppress the notification needed for continued servicing.
The output is directly driven by ctrl.enable, so clearing the setting removes the generated clock-enable request.
A bus write replaces ctrl.device_addr and a bus read exposes its stored value, while the setting is used for address acceptance.
The stored address comparison selects whether the engine enters S_RESP, so an altered address can reject intended transfers.
A bus write changes ctrl.fsel and the setting is read back and used to select the sampling tick.
ctrl.fsel selects clkgen_i(clk_div64_c) or clkgen_i(clk_div8_c), changing the sampling pace.
The selected sampling tick gates valid generation and movement of the synchronizer stages, so a bad selection can stop useful sampling.
A bus write changes ctrl.hide_read, and the setting is read back and used by the engine's addressed-read decision.
ctrl.hide_read together with tx_fifo.free determines whether an addressed read is suppressed or proceeds to S_RESP.
A bus write changes ctrl.tx_dummy_en, and the setting is read back and used to select the empty-transmit fallback.
This point computes the selected transmit data, but the RTL shows no independent unauthorized access to the policy at this downstream point.
Bus write data is presented to the transmit FIFO, where altered data can replace the intended payload.
The request strobe, direction, and address decide whether payload data is written, so they can suppress or redirect queuing.

points.reached by: the backward influence path from tx_fifo_inst storage
points.reason: The clear control can discard queued transmit payloads and prevent them from being sent.
By the black-box rule, the FIFO stores the write data and returns it through rdata; its write, read, and clear inputs can alter or block the queued payload.
The last transmitted FIFO byte is retained in tx_dummy and can be observed indirectly through later transmitted fallback data.

points.reached by: the tx_fifo_inst ==> engine.rdata and tx_backup ==> engine.rdata arrows
points.reason: The transmit byte is selected from FIFO data, retained data, or all ones before being loaded for transmission, so the selection can change or suppress the intended payload.
The selected transmit byte is loaded into the engine and shifted to twd_sda_o, where it can be disclosed, changed, or prevented from being sent.
Sampled SDA bits enter the receive path here, while enable and sampling controls can replace them with inactive values or stop sampling.
The sampled SDA history is converted into sda and start/stop events that determine whether received bits are processed.
The engine shifts sampled SDA into engine.sreg and can refuse a receive write when the RX FIFO is full.
The assembled received byte is presented as FIFO write data and can be changed before storage.
The engine decides whether the received byte is written, and a full FIFO can suppress that write.

points.reached by: the backward influence path from rx_fifo_inst storage
points.reason: Enable or clr_rx can clear the receive FIFO and thereby discard received payloads.
By the black-box rule, the FIFO stores assembled bytes and returns them through rdata; write, read, and clear controls can corrupt, expose, or discard them.
A bus read selects rx_fifo.rdata for return, while the read controls determine whether buffered data is removed and made available to the host.
Serial SDA bits enter the command path here, and sampling controls can alter or stop the command bit stream.
Start and stop events derived from sampled command traffic determine whether command processing begins or terminates.
The engine captures the command direction and address and uses them to select, abandon, receive, or transmit a transaction.
The captured command direction decides whether the engine stores received data.
The command direction and acknowledge condition decide whether transmit data is consumed.

points.reached by: the backward path from irq_trigger through ctrl.{enable,irq_rx_avail,irq_rx_full,irq_tx_empty}
points.reason: Bus writes can change the enable and interrupt-mask settings that determine whether required FIFO notifications are generated.
By the black-box rule, RX FIFO availability and fullness outputs can change the interrupt decision and can suppress required servicing.
By the black-box rule, the TX FIFO availability output controls the transmit-empty interrupt condition.
The process computes and registers irq_o from the enable masks and FIFO status, so its decision can be falsified or suppressed.
